messages:
deploy-bot: Rolling out micro-rollout v2.3 to thin-slice pool shard-7 -> 25% of traffic starting now. CI: green. :rocket:
amy.lee: copy, watching metrics. shard-7 dry-run looks fine earlier.
devon: getting an alert from synthetic checks, increased p95 on shard-7, +170ms. digging.
incident-bot: Paging @dan_oncall: high p95 latency on service/runtime - shard-7 (alert #RT-4521).
dan_oncall: on it, joining call. can someone paste the deployment change?
jess_m: this rollout flipped the new batching affinity kernel selector (kernel=affinity_v2) and thin-slice prefetch enabled for that slice. config diff: 
```
SERVING_KERNEL: affinity_v1 -> affinity_v2
PREFETCH_THINSLICES: false -> true
BATCH_WINDOW_MS: 4 -> 6
```
samir: seeing sawtooth throughput on the dashboards, throughput dips every ~30s with eviction spikes in the prefetch pool. KV miss rate up.
amy.lee: confirmed kernel fallback events in logs: "kernel_fallback: affinity_v2 -> affinity_v1 reason=latency_threshold" multiple times since 1780018830.
devon: so it's flipping kernels back and forth causing batch fragmentation and increased latency. probably new kernel interacts poorly with prefetch on thin slices.
dan_oncall: immediate mitigation options? rollback or kill the prefetch flag for shard-7. which is safer?
jess_m: kill-prefetch is low-risk and immediate. command: `redwood flags set PREFETCH_THINSLICES shard-7 false --env prod` (takes ~30s to propagate).
samir: +1 to kill-prefetch now, we can hold rollout while we analyze.
incident-bot: Action: flip flag PREFETCH_THINSLICES=false for shard-7 by amy.lee at 1780018905.
amy.lee: running flag flip now. `> redwood flags set PREFETCH_THINSLICES shard-7 false --yes`
deploy-bot: Flag change applied; propagation acknowledged by control plane at 1780018920.
devon: early signs good — p95 dropping back toward baseline, KV miss rate decreasing. still a few kernel fallback logs but frequency reduced.
dan_oncall: keeping traffic slice at 25% paused for further observation. who's owning full rollback if needed? jess?
jess_m: I can own rollback. If we need to rollback rollout entirely: `redwood rollout rollback micro-rollout v2.3 --shard shard-7 --confirm` — but prefer not unless back-and-forth persists.
samir: customer impact check: error rate stable, but latency increase impacted about 18% of in-flight requests on shard-7 during the peak window (1780018800-1780018920). Affected customers: two high-volume tenants saw increased tail latency; ops alerting CSM.
dan_oncall: good to know. I'll escalate to support: please prepare a short impact blurb for CSM. amy, can you draft?
amy.lee: draft: "We briefly observed elevated request latency for a subset of traffic routed to shard-7 after the micro-rollout. We disabled thin-slice prefetch for that shard which reduced the latency; no increased error rates observed. We're continuing to monitor; engineering is investigating kernel-selector interaction." Feel free to tweak.
devon: adding notes — root cause hypothesis: affinity_v2 increases micro-batching on thin slices which interacts badly with our eviction policy under certain sequence-length distributions, causing KV cache churn and kernel fallback.
jess_m: next steps: 1) keep flag off for shard-7 and finish canary in other shards with flag off, 2) run targeted load tests reproducing sequence-length mix, 3) revert kernel change or add fallback debounce if needed.
dan_oncall: handoff plan: I'll hand to devon for postmortem and follow-up after 30m observation window. If p95 stable (< +20ms) by 1780019240, we close paging.
incident-bot: Handoff: oncall -> devon at 1780019000.
samir: logging note: collected kernel traces + batch profiles, uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/rt-4521/1780018765 with tags.
amy.lee: leaving monitoring on this thread, marking incident state: mitigated (flag flipped), investigating. :white_check_mark:
jess_m: thanks all — if latency resurfaces we escalate to rollback.
adan: (typo in thread, no action)
